partners.mechanism_chain: PDGFRA (HGNC:8803) —DISRUPTS→ PDGF signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-190890); PDGF signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-190890) —LEADS_TO→ Gastrointestinal polyps (HP:0002670); PDGF signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-190890) —LEADS_TO→ Eosinophil proliferation and activation (GO:0002743); Eosinophil proliferation and activation (GO:0002743) —LEADS_TO→ Hypereosinophilia (HP:0001883). Gain-of-function mutations in PDGFRA lead to aberrant activation of the PDGF signaling pathway. This dysregulation drives uncontrolled mesenchymal cell proliferation, manifesting as gastrointestinal polyps (Disease A). Concurrently, the same aberrant PDGF signaling contributes to excessive eosinophil proliferation and activation, a hallmark of idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome (Disease B).

partners.mechanism_chain: PDGFRA (HGNC:9100) —INCREASES→ PDGF signaling pathway (R-HSA-1909773); PDGF signaling pathway (R-HSA-1909773) —LEADS_TO→ Gastrointestinal polyps (HP:0002670); IL2RB (HGNC:6045) —INCREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (R-HSA-176175); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (R-HSA-176175) —DISRUPTS→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (R-HSA-176175) —INCREASES→ Lymphoproliferation (HP:0002711); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (R-HSA-176175) —INCREASES→ Autoimmunity (HP:0001724). Gain-of-function mutations in PDGFRA lead to aberrant activation of the PDGF signaling pathway, promoting fibroid polyp formation in the gastrointestinal tract. Concurrently, gain-of-function mutations in IL2RB dysregulate the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, resulting in immune deficiency, lymphoproliferation, and autoimmunity. The convergence lies in the shared reliance on tightly regulated cell growth and immune signaling pathways, where dysregulation of either PDGF or JAK-STAT signaling can lead to distinct but mechanistically related pathologies.
